version.changelog: v5.1.5 — makes the launching-soon real mailing address beta explicit: street address + mailbox number, scan/photo intake, OCR/classification, agent notifications, and linked reply workflows.

llm.summary: The skill is a coherent postal-mail integration, but it gives agents real-world mail authority, including potentially destructive mailbox actions, without consistently requiring human approval.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the capabilities: remote MCP/REST access for sending physical mail, reading forwarded inbound mail context, and managing a private-beta mailbox workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Operational guidance includes automatic standing-instruction rules and examples such as junk mail discard, plus scan/forward/hold/shred/dispose/return actions, without a default approval requirement for destructive actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is a remote MCP server using bearer authentication; the optional npx mcp-remote bridge is disclosed and no local package code is included in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The access is high-impact because it can send physical mail, read sensitive inbound document context, create charges, and in beta workflows alter or destroy physical mail; safeguards exist but are not consistently mandatory.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses remote standing instructions, webhooks, notes, tags, and persistent metadata; these are purpose-aligned but should be treated as sensitive account state.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. Use sandbox or dry-run keys first, prefer agent-scoped keys, enable force_approval and spend limits, and do not allow autonomous shred, dispose, return-to-sender, discard, or outbound production mail unless a human has approved the specific rule and understands the legal, privacy, and cost impact.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] unexpected: The destructive mailbox actions are purpose-related, but the artifact documents shred/dispose/return and discard workflows as normal actions without consistently requiring operator confirmation.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The MAILBOX.md and decision-framework examples support the scanner concern because they can cause automatic discard of mail based on classification.
[SQP-2] expected: The install guide does disclose outbound physical mail, inbound forwarded document context, sandbox keys, and agent-scoped keys, so the data-access concern is partially mitigated but still under-warns about real-world consequences.
[suspicious.exposed_secret_literal] expected: The static scan appears to have matched placeholder API key examples such as sk_live_xxxxxxxxxxxxx, not an exposed live secret.
